title: YC 2026
method: Read from YC's public directory index through the daily yc-oss/api mirror. A company joins a group only if its own one-liner contains a phrase that supports it; the rest stay ungrouped.
overview: All 788 companies in YC's four 2026 batches. 640 fall into twelve groups; the other 148 don't share a clear group and are shown in grey.

groups.name: Agent and developer infrastructure
groups.rubric: Tools whose users are AI agents or the engineers who build and run software: sandboxes, payments, identity, memory, observability, coding agents, testing, DevOps.
groups.narration: 111 companies build infrastructure for AI agents and the engineers who run them: sandboxes, payments, identity, observability and coding agents. Agentcard lets agents buy things online, Orgo sells computers for agents, and Stage reviews code for humans and agents.

groups.name: Compute, chips and models
groups.rubric: Inference, GPUs, chips, model efficiency, or new models and AI research labs.
groups.narration: 47 companies work on compute, chips and models. Baud and Lamb Labs make AI chips, Expanse sells unused GPU capacity, and Ndea is building AGI.

groups.name: Data, evals and training environments
groups.rubric: Sells training data, evaluations, benchmarks, RL environments or simulations to the people who train models.
groups.narration: 44 companies sell data, evaluations or training environments to model builders. Markov sells computer-use data to frontier labs, Fern builds RL environments for robotics companies, and ARC Prize Foundation makes AI benchmarks.

groups.name: Robotics and physical AI
groups.rubric: Robots, their parts and the software that runs them, autonomous vehicles and civilian drones.
groups.narration: 50 companies build robots and the parts and software around them; 21 are from Summer. OS3 and Theseus Robotics make humanoids, Servo7 unloads containers in warehouses, and Silica makes actuators for physical AI.

groups.name: Operations agents
groups.rubric: AI that runs day-to-day operations for one industry or business function: construction, logistics, manufacturing, hospitality, legal, hiring, government.
groups.narration: 81 companies run day-to-day operations for one industry or business function. Bidflow and Rudus do construction takeoffs, Axelrod and Lance run hotels, and Walter runs manufacturing operations.

groups.name: Sales, marketing and support
groups.rubric: Sells, markets or supports customers for other businesses: sales agents, marketing content, advertising, customer support.
groups.narration: 44 companies sell, market or support customers for other businesses; 21 are from Spring. Corvera is an AI sales agent for CPG brands, Gojiberry builds go-to-market agents, and Cignara handles customer support.

groups.name: AI-native service firms
groups.rubric: Describes itself as the service provider (firm, practice, agency, brokerage, insurer, BPO, CRO) rather than software sold to one.
groups.narration: 47 companies describe themselves as the service firm itself, not software sold to one; 20 are from Summer. Billow and Rational are accounting firms, Vector Legal and Moritz are law firms, and Kinro is an insurance brokerage.

groups.name: Space, energy and manufacturing
groups.rubric: Space hardware, energy and power, data-center physical infrastructure, and advanced manufacturing.

groups.name: Finance and markets
